comparison_intro: Count ordinary discrete day, month and year boundaries. A one-day interval can cross a month or year, and reversed dates produce signed counts.

language_notes.sas: INTCK defaults to discrete intervals. Loader reads DATE9. values; macro retains the SAS date columns. SAS harness is unexecuted.
language_notes.python: parse_date9 maps English month names before pd.to_datetime. The copied frame holds datetime columns; .dt supplies calendar components.
language_notes.r: parse_date9 maps English month names to Date values. part(x, format) extracts integer calendar components; both helpers are in reference.R.

semantic_notes.title: Calendar boundaries, not durations
semantic_notes.text: Month counts come from year/month positions. Days divided by 30 and completed-anniversary calculations answer different questions.

semantic_notes.title: Date representations differ
semantic_notes.text: SAS dates, pandas datetimes and R Date values store dates differently. Compare calendar meaning and boundary counts, preserving row order.

tests.name: Original fixture: all 18 counts
tests.input: Original six start/end pairs, including Jan 31 -> Feb 1 and Dec 31 -> Jan 1.
tests.catches: Days/30 month estimates, elapsed-anniversary rules or incorrect year counting.

tests.name: Added calendar boundary probes
tests.input: Same date; next day in same month; Feb 29 -> Mar 1; Dec 31 -> Jan 1; reversed year boundary.
tests.catches: Off-by-one counts, leap-month mistakes, loss of sign and fixed-length month approximations.

tests.name: Preserve dates, types and order
tests.input: All CSV pairs in reverse order with custom row identifiers.
tests.expected: Inputs untouched; output dates retain calendar meaning; counts numeric; row order and all expected results preserved.
tests.catches: Date truncation, input mutation, sorting, text result columns or position-dependent answers.

scope: Valid English DATE9 inputs; date-only ordinary discrete day/month/year intervals, including same-date and reverse-direction probes. Continuous, shifted, multiplied, custom and datetime intervals are excluded.
